title: Zhihu CEO Zhou Yuan Responds to Indirect Investment in DeepSeek: This Is a Well-Researched Long-Term Strategic Decision

content_html:
Zhihu has used real money to invest indirectly in DeepSeek, and shareholders are bound to ask: Why invest when the company is losing money? On November 25, CEO Zhou Yuan responded on the earnings call: this investment is a long-term strategic decision made after thorough research and prudent evaluation, and the company “has a very clear judgment” about its strategic goals, capital arrangements, and long-term value.

It’s an Investment in the AI Ecosystem, Not a Gamble

On November 23, Zhihu issued a voluntary announcement: the Tianjin Lisi Xingshen Equity Investment Partnership, in which the company is an investor, has indirectly invested in DeepSeek through an intermediary entity, obtaining a low single-digit percentage equity stake.

Zhou Yuan defined this move as “participating in AI ecosystem building from a broader industry perspective,” exploring long-term industrial synergy and value creation. He said the company had fully considered its cash reserves and future operating needs, and that the investment would not have a material adverse impact on normal operations and core business, nor would it come at the expense of its main business, financial soundness, or shareholders’ long-term interests; buybacks will still be resolutely carried out.

Q3 Report: Revenue Flat, Loss Slightly Wider

Behind the earnings call is a financial report that is not easy: third-quarter revenue was RMB 659 million, flat year over year; gross margin was 57.2%, down 4.1 percentage points year over year, due to continued expansion of content supply and user investment. By segment, marketing services revenue was RMB 198 million, up 4.5% year over year; paid content and IP operations were RMB 394 million, roughly flat; vocational training revenue declined amid strategic optimization.

Net loss attributable to shareholders was RMB 49.583 million, widening 6.28% year over year. On the expense side, the company tightened: total operating expenses were RMB 488 million, down 3.1% year over year, while R&D expenses bucked the trend and rose 9.3%—cutting operating costs on one hand, ramping up R&D on the other, and squeezing out money to bet on AI; the calculation is very clear.
